title: Setting up MAXQDA and Key Terms
text:
This section demonstrates how to use MAXQDA with the license provided by the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign for current students, faculty, and staff.
If you’re not with the university, you can access MAXQDA by signing up for a free trial or purchasing your own license.


If you haven’t yet, download the MAXQDA program to you Mac or Windows computer. Follow the usual procedures for installing software on your device.






TipUse MAXQDA via Illinois AnyWare if you can’t install on your device



If you cannot, or do not want to install the MAXQDA software on your compute, you can use the University’s virtual desktop service Illinois AnyWare. This service lets you access a Windows desktop from your own device and use the software installed on that desktop without having to add them to your own device.





Open the program. The first time you open MAXQDA on a new device, you will need to set the license information. You should see a screen (Figure 1) that says Welcome to MAXQDA and then asks you to choose a license option.
Click on the option that says Connect to your institution's network license






Figure 1






After you choose to make use of an institutional license, you’ll be prompted to enter the license details (Figure 2).

In the first box asks for your institution’s server address. Enter: maxqda.webstore.illinois.edu
Set the Port to 21990
Make sure the radio button for the last box is checked and enter the license name MAXQDA (all caps included).
Click Connect







License information added




Figure 2









ImportantUsing MAXQDA off campus?



If you are working off-campus, you will need to be connected to the campus network via the Virtual Private Network (VPN). Once you have connected to the VPN, the steps for accessing MAXQDA remain the same.
Technology Services offers instructions for setting up the VPN.





In addition to the network license, you may choose to log into the MAXQDA program with a (free) MAXQDA account. This account is not connected to your Illinois license, and you can use any email you prefer.
You only need to connect a license if you want to use the AI-Assist features (which is included in the Illinois license) or any of the other add-on features that can be purchased from MAXQDA, including automated transcription and Team Cloud tools.
To link a MAXQDA account:

Create an account on the MAXQDA website.
Look for the Sign In option in the upper right corner of the program. (Figure 3 (a))
Enter your account details. (Figure 1)












(a) Sign in option (upper right in MAXQDA)








Enter your log in details






Figure 3: Logging in to a MAXQDA account within the program.

title: Setting up MAXQDA and Key Terms
text:
Interface elements
Once you are logged in you and created a new project (see Creating a New Project for more information), you will see the MAXQDA program itself. There are four different windows1 within the program (Figure 5) that you will need to know. MAXQDA uses specific vocabulary terms throughout the software to describe parts of a qualitative project and it will be easier to conduct your own research with a strong grasp of this language.
The four windows are:

Document system: The data files you upload will be stored here.
Code system: The codes you add to the project will be listed here.
Document browser: This window displays the data document that you have selected.
Retrieved segments: This window displays the data at the intersection of activated documents and codes. See more on activation.







A new project in MAXQDA with all four workspace windows open.




Figure 5
crumbs: Setting up MAXQDA and Key Terms

title: Setting up MAXQDA and Key Terms
text:
Activation
MAXQDA uses activation2 to help you focus on a subset of the data at the intersection of the activated codes and data documents. Once you have activated both data and code(s), you will see the matching data in the retrieved segments window.

How would you use activation to analyze qualitative data?
For a set of data with with interviews and teachers about school-family communication, we have coded the interview data with examples of positive communication experiences:

Activate the documents for teachers
Activate codes related to positive communication

The retrieved segment window would then show us just the data that meets those two conditions.
We might then change the document activation to focus on parents instead.
By comparing the two sets of retrieved segments, we can start examining whether there are differences or similarities in how these two groups see positive school-family communication.

title: Creating a new project in MAXQDA
text:
When you first open MAXQDA, you’ll be prompted tho choose what project file you want to work with.
The three options are to:

Create an entirely new project.
Open an existing MAXQDA project.
Create a file that contains example data for exploring MAXQDA features.









The opening screen of MAXQDA where you can (1) create a new project (2) open an existing project or (3) open a file with example data.




Figure 1








After you choose to create a new project, you’ll be prompted to choose where you want the project file to be stored.


You choose where to store your project file and any data you upload to MAXQDA. If you save the project file in a shared folder or cloud service, then the shared settings of those locations will also apply to your data.
You should choose a storage location that meets any data security and confidentiality protections required by the IRB application or project design.






WarningSaving to external or cloud storage?



MAXQDA recommends that you do not open a project file directly form an external storage system like a networked drive, flash drive, or a cloud storage service (like OneDrive, Box, or Google Drive).
If your project and data files are stored in cloud storage, they recommend instead that you make a copy of the file to save directly to your local device. When you have completed your work you can re-upload the project file to the cloud storage.





MAXQDA keeps larger data files in a separate folder that allows the data to be accessible for analysis, but without making the project file itself too large. The external file location is the same for all MAXQDA projects, but can be a location you choose.



Open MAXQDA > Preferences to change the external file settings.

By default, any file over 5MB is saved as an external file. You can change this limit to be larger or smaller.
You can change the location for external files by clicking on the ... button and then choosing a new location on your device.









Open the MAXQDA preferences to set the size for files to be saved external storage and the external file location




Figure 2






Next: Adding data to your project file

section: Existing highlights or comments in Word or PDF documents
text:
Existing highlights or comments in Word or PDF documents
If you upload Word or PDF documents that have existing highlighted portions or comments, those will be imported into your MAXQDA project along with the data files.






Example of codes created when uploaded Word or PDF documents with highlights.




Figure 3



Highlighted sections will be coded with the color of the highlight, with MAXQDA creating a new code labeled with the color name. You can change the name of the color to a descriptive term if you would like.
Comments will be added and appear in the left side of the document.

title: Jess Hagman
text: Hi, I’m Jess Hagman, a librarian at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. This site is where i share the materials that I’ve created for teaching qualitative data analysis and other public materials from my work.

title: web
section: Types of research findings or outcomes
text:
Types of research findings or outcomes

Frequencies or counts
Topical surveys
Thematic
Theories or explanations
Ethnographic description

title: web
text:
Describing your methods and values

Qualitative is a big category, with lots of different types of data, analysis strategies, and ideas about what “quality” looks like. (Small & Calarco, 2022). Under this “Big Tent” (Tracy, 2025) of qualitative research, it can be hard for new researchers to find their place and what makes their research credible to readers. (Roulston & Bhattacharya, 2018)
When readers have different ideas about what makes research high quality, you may receive feedback or evaluation that is based on different assumptions about rigor. (Clarke et al., 2025; Moura et al., 2025).
To counter this challenge, your paper should explain how you analyzed the data and what you believe makes the analysis credible. (Smagorinsky, 2008; Staller & Krumer-Nevo, 2013)

title: web
section: Sorting data into groups or variables
text:
Sorting data into groups or variables
The concept of variables is used more frequently in quantitative research, but we can use this language to think of groups within the data that we want to use for comparison in order to answer our research questions.1
Variables can be:

pre-existing: such as types of data, groups of participants, research sites, or phases of data collection
or, identified as you analyze and applied to the data for comparisons, such as when you identify a group of participants who have an experience relevant to your research questions.


❓ What existing groups or variables are there in your data?

I use variables here because this is the term used in MAXQDA, the QDA software available on campus.

title: web
section: Transcribing data from media to text formats
text:
Transcribing data from media to text formats








The practice of transforming audio or video content into text for the purposes of analysis.
Potential tools:

Meeting software transcripts (e.g. Zoom, Teams)
Transcription software (Trint, Otter)
Manual transcription support - provides tools to facilitate typing what you hear (e.g. MAXQDA, oTranscribe)
Illinois Mediaspace - create and edit a transcription of uploaded media.

title: web
text:
Coding




Labeling segments of the data with a topic, concept, or other descriptor. These codes allow us to look up from the specifics of individuals or cases and look across the data to identify patterns. (Richards, 2021)
While coding is used in many qualitative methods, it is not a required element of every qualitative project. (Coffey, 1996; Saldaña, 2025).
Coding can be done using analog versions of your data, with ordinary productivity software, or software developed specifically for qualitative data analysis (sometimes called CAQDAS or QDAS).

title: web
text:
Analyzing coded data
Once you have coded your data, you can use the coded data set to ask further questions about the data and move towards research findings.

title: web
text:
Writing
Across qualitative texts, you’ll find a frequent recommendation to write throughout the process of collecting and analyzing data.
Writing has you work has several benefits, including:

Writing as thinking: Sometimes writing out an explanation serves as a way of thinking through a challenge or question in a way that just internal pondering cannot.(Keane, 2022; Montgomery & Bailey, 2007)
Writing as documentation: Have a record of how you analyzed the data and how your interpretation developed will help you write about that process and communicate the quality of your analysis.(Kalpokas & Radivojevic, 2022)
Writing as kindness to your future self: The version of yourself who writes the paper or dissertation that comes out of this analysis will appreciate having as much previously written information as possible. You may be able to edit and use your memos or other writing in your final product.

title: Workshop: Introduction to MAXQDA
text:
Welcome
This workshop is for those new to MAXQDA. It covers:

Accessing the University of Illinois license for MAXQDA (for those at UIUC)
Create a project file and setting file locations
An overview of the interface and key terms you’ll need to use MAXQDA effectively
Adding commonly used data types into your MAXQDA project, including interview transcripts, text files, survey data, and media files.
Creating codes and applying them to text data.
